status: The crew's voices (roadmap 8.10, docs/crew/10_BODIES_AND_VOICES.md), read by simcore/crew_voice.hpp: what a speech engine says for each callout and in whose voice. Recorded lines, where there are any, take the place of the engine's (unreal/README.md).
source: sam3d estimates: presentation, chosen by ear so each crew's five seats can be told apart (the Osa's and the PU-12M's; the operator and the driver sound alike in both)
notes: Pitch and rate are on the speech engine's -10..10 scale (Windows SAPI's absmiddle and absspeed). The language is the first of 'languages' that the player's machine has a voice for: Russian needs a Russian voice (Windows: Settings > Time & language > Speech > Add voices > Russian), otherwise the English lines are spoken. The rates are a little fast: the crew speaks briskly, and the simulation gives a line 0.4 s plus 0.35 s a word (crew_callouts.hpp), quicker than a speech engine's normal pace.

seats.notes: The senior voice in the cabin.
The PU-12M: the battery commander in his post, the senior voice there.
The PU-12M's squad leader (the vehicle's commander).
The battery commander on the battery net (an R-123M).

stress.source: sam3d estimate: a stressed crewman speaks higher and faster

bands.source: sam3d estimate: a telephone-quality channel for the R-124 intercom, a narrower one for the R-123M's VHF FM voice, a voice across the compartment nearly full-band

ru.source: sam3d: the Russian letter names (а, бэ, вэ, гэ ...) for initialisms read aloud letter by letter; СОЦ is said as a word
